title: kernel nightshift checklist — Clara
content:
Quick context / purpose:
- Night shift scratchpad for kernel-level triage. Keep short, actionable, copy/paste-friendly.
- Goal: stabilize p99 regression on small requests path (seq len 8–32).

Recent observed behavior (last 24h):
- Baseline p99 for small requests ~52ms (steady).
- Spike window: 02:10–03:40 UTC — p99 jumps to 200–320ms for ~15m, then intermittent bumps for next hour.
- CPU side traces show kernel wait spikes on worker threads servicing KV cache lookups.
- Affected service: serving-runtime-gpu-prod-a (nv-rt-3) on region-us-west-2.

Immediate triage checklist (do these first):
- [ ] Check recent deploys / rollouts (last 2 hours). Command: 
    gcloud run revisions list --filter="service=serving-runtime-gpu-prod-a" --format="table(name,createTime)" | tail -n 10
- [ ] Inspect SLO-alerts page + incidents: https://console.redwood/slo/serving-runtime/p99
- [ ] Look at kernel ooms / dmesg on host suspected: ssh ops@nv-rt-3; sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 500
- [ ] Capture top and perf during an active spike window: sudo perf top -p $(pgrep runtime_worker) -g --no-children (leave running for 30s)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache lock contention under thin requests due to unexpected cache misses causing sync fetches (most likely).
2) Microbatch scheduling jitter: batcher wakes and serializes requests into a slow path for small sequences.
3) CUDA/NUMA imbalance leads to bursts where a subset of worker threads stall on memory migration.
4) New kernel patch on host bumped scheduler behavior (less likely but check host patches).

Quick experiments to run (non-invasive):
- EXP-A: Force async fetch fallback to measure latency delta. Add env var on one replica: RUNTIME_FORCE_ASYNC_KV=true. Watch for p95/p99 change only on that instance.
- EXP-B: Reduce max_batch_delay to 2ms on a canary replica to see if latency smooths for small seqs. Config: serving-runtime/canary-3 route.
- EXP-C: Temporarily disable KV LRU GC to check whether eviction is thrashing. (Only on isolated canary).

Commands / snippets (save for copying):
- Check recent kernel logs (host): sudo journalctl -k -n 500 | grep -i stall || true
- Get runtime worker thread pids: ps aux | grep runtime_worker | awk '{print $2}'
- Perf script snapshot: sudo perf record -F 200 -p $PID -g -- sleep 15; sudo perf script | c++filt | head -n 200 > /tmp/perf-snap.txt
- Dump kv-cache stats endpoint: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9102/debug/kv-cache | jq '.'

Notes to self (observations I saw):
- When I hit the /debug/kv-cache endpoint during a spike, hit rate dropped to 0.34 (from usual ~0.92). Eviction rate doubled.
- One worker process showed long syscall wait times (futex) matching p99 spikes.
- The host had an unmerged kernel update staged but not rebooted (check apt history).

TL;DR quick runbook for night:
1) Identify whether a deploy correlates with window. If yes -> rollback candidate -> talk to release-eng.
2) If no deploy, enable EXP-A on single canary. Wait 10m.
3) If EXP-A fixes p99 -> root cause likely kv-cache sync miss path -> follow PR template below.
4) If EXP-A no change, try EXP-B. If EXP-B reduces latency but lowers throughput -> tune batcher heuristics.

Longer-term follow ups / ticket notes (write to JIRA once confirmed):
- RINF-4721: "Investigate KV cache eviction + futex contention causing p99 spikes" (draft)
    - Attach perf flamegraphs, kv-cache dump, host dmesg.
    - Owner: Clara. Expected ETA for fix: 1–2 sprints (hotfix may be backported).
- Potential improvement: add async contagion path for cache miss that doesn't hold global lock.

Owner TODOs (my checklist):
- [ ] Run EXP-A canary tonight and monitor for 30m. (assign: Clara)
- [ ] If EXP-A passes, open PR with simple async fetch flag and a unit test that simulates concurrent misses. (assign: Clara)
- [ ] If EXPA fails, run perf recording during spike and attach to RINF-4721. (assign: Clara)
- [ ] Ping release-eng if a rollback is required. Slack: @release-eng.

Unresolved questions / what to ask the oncall backup:
- Did any infra autoscaler events coincide with the spike? (ask infra team)
- Any memory pressure events in monitoring (OOM killer logs) we missed?

Small ergonomics notes for future:
- Add a quick /debug/kv-cache?short endpoint that returns just hit/evict/hit_rate to avoid heavy dumps during spikes.
- Consider exposing futex wait histograms in runtime telemetry when compiled with +futex-stats flag.

Random brain-dumps (these are fuzzy, carry low priority):
- Maybe we should add a background thread that prefetches predicted keys for short prompts (cheap heuristic).
- Try switching to shared_mutex for read-mostly kv access if contention is confirmed.

If I get paged: immediate script to reduce blast radius:
- curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/replica-scale -d 'service=serving-runtime-gpu-prod-a&replicas=1' (scale down heavy path)
- Set route weight of canary to 100% if canary proves stable: admin-route-update --service serving-runtime --route small-requests --weight canary-3:100

End-of-shift notes (to fill before handing off):
- What I did, what I saw, next steps. Short and explicit.

---
Last quick snapshot (03/13/2026 05:12 UTC):
- Started EXP-A on canary at 04:50 UTC. After 12m p99 reduced from ~280ms -> 60ms on canary only.
- Global cluster still showing intermittent events but amplitude down.
- Next action: open RINF-4721 with perf + kv dump and request micro-release for async fetch flag on 1 more node.
